## Question

<div class="chapter-question">If a group of agents converges on a good answer, what evidence shows that interaction produced the result?</div>

## Why this week belongs here

Week 9 specifies interaction. Week 10 asks how to attribute a collective result when the same endpoint might come from shared model priors, leakage, prompting or selection of a favorable run.

## Provisional core readings

- Barrie et al. (2026), §§10.4.4–10.4.5. [Download chapter PDF](../downloads/readings/ai-and-research-methods-barrie-et-al-2026.pdf). [@BarrieEtAl2026AIResearchMethods]
- Ashery, Aiello and Baronchelli (2025), “Emergent Social Conventions and Collective Bias in LLM Populations.” [@AsheryAielloBaronchelli2025]
- Barrie and Törnberg (2025), “Emergent LLM Behaviors Are Observationally Equivalent to Data Leakage.” [@BarrieTornberg2025]
- Further comparison: Kim et al. (2026) and Chuang et al. (2024). [@KimEtAlSocieties2026; @ChuangEtAl2024]

## Planned chapter and class arc

Distinguish convergence from correctness; compare repeated runs and no-interaction baselines; introduce observational equivalence; evaluate contamination probes and alternative explanations for collective performance.

[See the provisional Week 10 Python plan](../python/session10.qmd).
